content:
What a hell of a job to take off and put on the pully.
By the second one (Y-ax) I used some WD-40 between the shaft and the pully to put it off and the new one on and that worked well.

replies.content: I had the same problem but mine got stuck on halfway and ended destroying it taking it off. Had to order a replacement and reamed out the new one for it to fit. Plus a little WD-40 to get it on.

content:
If you are upgrading an INDX machine, make sure that after the four screws are through the frame and into the motor, the motor/mount assembly is positioned as far forward (towards the front of the printer) as possible before tightening the 4 screws. There is a small amount of play in the location of the motor within the bent-metal frame and the indexing holes.

If you loosely assemble the motor/mounts without pushing them fully forward, you may run into dock calibration issues, like I did with tools 1–2 and 7–8.

Both motor/mount assemblies should be pushed as far forward as possible within the indexing holes before tightening everything down. This will help prevent dock calibration issues.
I was able to do this section without cutting the zip tie, but it was more difficult. Your choice.
